events.text: The elders of the defeated sect come to your gate on foot, without their swords. The eldest sets a chest of silver on the bottom step and recites the oath of a vassal in a voice that does not shake. Every one of your disciples is on the wall to watch.

choices.text: Raise the eldest to their feet before the oath is finished

effects.log: You take the old elder by the arm before the last words. The defeated look at each other. Some of them will remember this longer than the war.

choices.text: Let them kneel until the last word is spoken

effects.log: You let the oath run its course in the cold. When it ends, nobody on either side of the gate is in any doubt about who won.

events.text: The first tribute of your new vassal arrives with the spring carts: silver, medicine, a crate of old manuals and a letter that is very careful with its words. The steward asks where to put it all, and whether to send a reply.

choices.text: Send back a gift worth a tenth of it

effects.log: You send a gift of 50 taels back down the road with a courteous letter. A vassal treated well is slower to remember its pride.

choices.text: Keep every coin and send no reply

effects.log: The steward counts it all into the treasury. Silence is a reply too, and the vassal will read it.

events.text: The plaque of the defeated sect is taken down from its own gate and carried into your great hall under a cloth. Hundreds of its disciples stand in rows in your courtyard, unpicking their old sleeve badges with their own hands. Some of them are crying. Some of them are watching you.

choices.text: Hang their old plaque in your hall, below your own

effects.log: You hang the old plaque in your hall, below your own, where everyone can see it. It is not the same as mercy, but the new disciples bow a little lower as they pass it.

choices.text: Have the old plaque split for firewood in front of them

effects.log: The plaque burns in the courtyard brazier. Nobody in the rows says a word. Nobody will forget whose sect they belong to now.

events.text: The library of the absorbed sect comes up your mountain on forty mules. Your eldest disciple walks beside the carts, reading the labels on the manual boxes aloud as if they were the names of the dead. A messenger waits at the gate with word that the other sects have closed their roads to your people.

choices.text: Open the new library to every disciple, old and new alike

effects.log: You open the library to everyone wearing your badge, whatever badge they wore before. By the next season the new disciples are arguing about the manuals with the old ones, which is a start.

choices.text: Lock the best manuals away for your own study

effects.log: You keep the key to the best shelf on your own belt. The halls notice which doors stay locked.

events.text: The tribute carts from your vassal never arrive. Instead a single rider comes to the gate, sets the seal of the vassal oath on the bottom step, broken cleanly in two, and rides away before anyone can stop them.

choices.text: Pick up the two halves and keep them on your desk

effects.log: You keep the broken seal where you can see it. A debt like that is easier to collect when you never forget it.

choices.text: Let the steward sweep the pieces away

effects.log: The pieces go out with the morning sweepings. There will be other vassals, and other years.

events.text: In the middle of the night the gate guard comes to wake you. A long line of lanterns is moving down the mountain road: the people of a sect you absorbed, carrying their old plaque wrapped in cloth. They are not running. They are walking home.

choices.text: Stand on the wall and let them go

effects.log: You watch the lanterns until the last of them goes round the bend. In the morning the halls are emptier, and quieter, and nobody mentions the night.

choices.text: Send riders after them with an offer to come back

effects.log: Your riders catch them at the ford with 100 taels and promises. Only a few turn back. The rest keep walking, and the murim hears that you asked.

events.text: From the palace terrace you can see the banners of every sect that is left in the murim, and every one of them is your own. The seal of the empire is on the table beside your sword. Below, the courtyard is full of officials and disciples who have never had to stand in the same place before, and none of them is quite sure where to look.

choices.text: Bow to the empty sky, as if someone were still above you

effects.log: You bow to the sky. It does not bow back, but the people in the courtyard see you do it, and they breathe a little easier.

choices.text: Raise the sword and the seal together, so the whole courtyard sees

effects.log: You raise them both. The roar from the courtyard comes up the steps like weather. Somewhere in it, quieter, are the people who are already counting the years until it ends.

events.text: The news reaches you at dusk: the hand that held the sword and the seal together is open again. Somewhere a new gate has been raised that is not yours, or the throne is in other hands. The palace is very quiet, and the sect halls are quieter still.

choices.text: Begin again, and write down how it was lost

effects.log: You write it all down that night, the mistakes first. It is a short list, and every line of it can be mended.

choices.text: Let it go: no one holds the whole sky for long

effects.log: You let it go. The night is warm, and for the first time in years nobody is waiting for your word.
